body:
I have previously tried this too. It turns out that it's actually not a UCM problem with device detection (the mic jack is supposed to be routed through line-in) but rather a Chip initialization problem. It seems as tho the chip is just waking up in a random state after a full (hard or long) power-cycle. The UCM driver in this instance seems to actually be operating perfectly fine because from the Kernel perspective that input is in fact not connected but the chip seems to just be routing the mic output to some random input port (without it's Windows Driver).
Take this explanation with a grain of salt because it genuinely is just my best guess from the behavior I have seen.
Note that opening those ports does seem to increase the chance of you getting a state that is "usable" (although the Audio quality does seem to decrease significantly if it's not bound to Line-in).
